newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr holds gains against yen, Eurostocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr holds gains against yen, Eurostocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar rallied against the yen on Thursday after officials on both sides of the Pacific talked it up, though it was off its best levels by midday, while European stock markets were mixed.
The dollar charged higher to stand near 116 yen in early European trade, over two yen up from late Wednesday, as Japanese and U.S. officials continued to will the U.S. currency higher.
"The comments by the Japanese that the yen has gone too far and too fast and rates are not going up are finally filtering through," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
The Japanese government has been battling to give the dollar a leg-up after it sank to five-month lows of 111.88 yen on Tuesday on expectations that Japan may soon raise interest rates.
The dollar stood at 115.85 yen at around 1100 gmt against 113.65 in late Europe on Wednesday.

"Certainly, Japanese policy makers appear keen to inject a note of calm into the market, and speculation about an imminent rate hike from the BoJ (Bank of Japan) also appears to be abating," said Paul Meggyesi, currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts said the dollar also appeared well bid after finding a floor below 112 yen earlier this week. "The comments have become a bit more urgent," said Ferridge.

In the latest round of verbal intervention, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said it agreed with the BoJ's low interest-rate policy and that concerns about excessive yen weakness were now completely gone.
Earlier, Takashini Anzai, executive director of the BoJ, said: "Correction to the yen's excessive weakness has begun, but the pace has been too rapid."
Some support for the ailing dollar was also received after U.S. Trade Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated the U.S. strong-dollar policy.

But the dollar was nearly a pfennig down from highs above 1.70 marks at midday in Europe, when it stood at 1.6915 marks little changed from Wednesday's European close, after an Ifo report showed German business confidence was strong.
Dollar/mark was also capped after Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said he saw no need to change German interest rates and that inflation prospects for the current year were favourable.
Share prices in London and Paris both opened lower but while London rallied Paris fell further. German shares opened higher before turning lower.

At 1100 gmt London's FTSE index was up 14.7 points at 4,656,7, while in Paris the CAC blue-chip index was down 40.13 points, or 1.44 percent at 2,746.22 and Germany's DAX was down 15.79 at 3,580.30 points.
London's FTSE 100 reversed early losses after data showing strong consumer demand and economic growth cheered the market, dealers and strategists said.

"People have accepted the fact that rates are going to go up and now they think that the sooner rates are raised the more chance of keeping inflation under control. In that way the figures were reasonably positive," said a senior dealer.
Britain's April retail sales rose a monthly 0.1 percent and yearly 4.7 percent against expectations of a monthly 0.3 percent and a yearly 4.1 percent.
First quarter GDP rose 0.9 percent quarterly and three percent yearly versus expectations of 1.0 percent quarterly and matching expectations of three percent yearly.
French shares traded lower with investors taking profits ahead of the end of the trading month on Friday and due to rumours related to the election, traders said.

"There is talk in the market of a secret poll which gives the right a small majority," said a head trader at a German bank in Paris. "But the problem with secret polls is that nobody has really seen them," he added.
There is a ban on the publication of opinion polls during this last week before the first round in the parliamentary election on May 25.
But financial firms and political parties are nevertheless ordering private polls from the polling institutes.

In Frankfurt, German shares were lower at midday after reversing early gains made when the DAX index raced to a new trading high at 3,612.67 points on the back of two economic reports which showed inflation remained little threat and the economy was gaining steam.
The Ifo economic research institute said its April west German business climate index jumped to 94.7 from 92.6, higher than expected.
The Bundesbank announced that M3 money supply grew an annualised 6.7 percent in April versus the average for the fourth quarter of 1996, lower than expectations.
STOCK PRICES AT 1100 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 14.7 points at 4,656.7.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 40.13 points at 2,746.22.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 15.79 at 3,580.30.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6915 marks and 115.85 yen compared with 1.6918 marks and 113.65 yen in late European trade on Wednesday.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1100 GMT
Gold fixed at $342.95 an ounce compared with $342.65 an ounce at Wednesday's close in London.
